scenario: A 58-year-old male presents with progressive shortness of breath over the past 3 months, a chronic cough producing whitish sputum, and a 40 pack-year smoking history. Spirometry shows FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.62 (below the 0.70 threshold). Chest X-ray shows hyperinflation.
explanation: The combination of a heavy smoking history, obstructive spirometry pattern (FEV1/FVC < 0.70), chronic productive cough, and hyperinflation is classic for COPD.
